title: Platform systems & services: dashboards, alerts, runbooks, retrospective & roadmap — Q2 2026
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary:

This document consolidates the platform team’s operational surface for Q2 2026: the canonical list of production dashboards, alerting rules and thresholds, standardized runbooks for common outage classes, a short retrospective for incidents in the quarter, and the team roadmap for the next two quarters. Use this page as the single source of truth for on-call actions, dashboard ownership, and planned platform improvements.

Sections:
1) Overview & scope
2) Dashboards (catalog + owners)
3) Alerts & thresholds (prometheus rules + intent)
4) Runbooks (triage and recovery steps)
5) Retrospective (Q2 incidents, metrics, learnings)
6) Roadmap & action items (owners + dates)
7) Team wiki links and how-tos

---

1) Overview & scope

- Scope: All platform-managed systems and services that support Redwood’s hosted API, Dedicated control plane, and internal infra orchestration (k8s clusters, GPU fleet schedulers, request router, cache layer, metrics pipeline, and deployment automation).
- Primary on-call focus: latency SLOs for inference (< p95 180ms for small models; < p95 400ms for large models on hosted tier), API error rate SLO (<= 0.1% 5m), and control-plane availability (99.95% monthly).
- Responsibilities: maintain dashboards, own alert definitions, keep runbooks up-to-date, run post-incident actions.

---

2) Dashboards (catalog + owners)

Note: all dashboards live in Grafana under the "Platform / Systems & Services" folder. Each entry below lists the dashboard, primary owner, and critical panels.

- Platform Overview — owner: Hana Rivera
  - Critical panels: global request rate, 99/95/50 latency by model class, error rate, successful tokens/s, total inference tokens billed
  - Pager panels: API error anomaly, model routing errors

- GPU Fleet Capacity — owner: Marcus Lee
  - Panels: free GPU pool count, node-level GPU memory pressure, pod eviction rate, scheduling queue length, preemption events
  - Use: capacity planning, Dedicated scaling decisions

- Request Router & Smart Routing — owner: Daniel Kim
  - Panels: per-route latency, route-level drop rate, fallback rate (percent requests routed to fallback model), routing decision heatmap

- Cache & Batching (KV Cache) — owner: Aisha Patel
  - Panels: cache hit ratio (prefix + KV), batch size distribution, batching latency vs standalone latency, cache evictions/sec

- Model Serving Runtime — owner: Sofia Martinez
  - Panels: per-model token generation rate, KV cache memory usage, attention kernel failure count, kernel fallback occurrences

- Observability / Metrics Pipeline — owner: Ravi Shah
  - Panels: prometheus scrape success rate, metrics ingestion lag, series cardinality, alert evaluation time

For each dashboard the owner must:
- Maintain panel queries and threshold annotations.
- Update dashboard README with recent changes.
- Review alert-to-panel mappings quarterly.

---

3) Alerts & thresholds (prometheus rules + intent)

This section enumerates high-priority alerts the on-call should treat as page-worthy vs. warnings for slack-only. Names follow the convention prom_ (service)_(signal)_(level).

Table: critical alerts

| alert_name | intent | threshold | page? | primary_responder | escalation |
| prom_api_error_rate_critical | API error rate spike | >0.5% errors over 5m | PagerDuty P0 | Platform-API on-call | Team lead -> Eng SRE -> CTO |
| prom_inference_p95_latency_high | API latency regression | p95 > 600ms for 3m | PagerDuty P0 | Platform-runtime on-call | Runtime lead -> Eng SRE |
| prom_gpu_pool_exhausted | GPU capacity exhausted | free_gpus < 3 in pool for 10m | PagerDuty P1 | GPU-fleet on-call | Infra lead -> VP Eng |
| prom_kv_cache_eviction_spike | Cache thrashing | evictions/sec > 500 for 2m | PagerDuty P1 | Platform-runtime on-call | Platform lead |
| prom_metrics_pipeline_lag | Obs pipeline lag | ingestion_lag > 2m | PagerDuty P2 | Observability on-call | Ravi Shah -> Platform lead |

Operational intent: page-worthy alerts indicate immediate customer impact (elevated errors, sustained large latency regressions, capacity exhaustion). Lower-severity alerts (e.g., moderate increase in batch latency) notify Slack and should be reviewed during business hours.

Alert tuning guidance:
- Use anomaly detection (prometheus recorded rules + Thanos Ruler annotations) for seasonal traffic.
- Set alert windows to avoid paging on short spikes: prefer 3m-10m depending on signal.
- Configure runbook links in alert annotations.

---

4) Runbooks (standardized triage and recovery)

General notes: runbooks are short, prescriptive, and tested in game days. Keep steps numbered and idempotent. Include rollback commands and quick tests (curl examples).

Runbook: API error-rate spike (prom_api_error_rate_critical)
1) Acknowledge the page in PagerDuty.
2) Confirm scope: run query for error rate by route/model over last 15m (Grafana quicklink).
3) Check recent deploys: kubectl get deployments --namespace=redwood --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp -o wide | head -n 20
4) If a recent rollout exists (< 30m), roll back the rollout: kubectl rollout undo deployment/<service> --namespace=redwood.
5) If no deploy, check request router for fallback rate and routing failures (Grafana panel).
6) If error is downstream (runtime/kernel failures), scale runtime replicas: kubectl scale deployment/runtime-workers --replicas=<current+2> --namespace=redwood; monitor token generation.
7) If mitigated, create incident in Incident repo, capture root cause hypothesis, and file a postmortem link.

Runbook: GPU pool exhaustion (prom_gpu_pool_exhausted)
1) Acknowledge page and check pool health: curl -s https://fleet.internal/api/v1/pools/<pool>/status
2) Determine if nodes are NotReady or unschedulable. kubectl get nodes -l gpu=true -o wide
3) If nodes are NotReady due to driver crash, follow driver restart: ssh node -> sudo systemctl restart nvidia-driver.service (see onprem packaging doc for details).
4) If OOM eviction/pressure, increase node autoscaler target or temporarily divert non-critical workloads to Dedicated burst pool.
5) Open a support ticket to cloud provider when hardware failure is suspected.

Runbook: Metrics ingestion lag (prom_metrics_pipeline_lag)
1) Check prometheus-write latency and object store write errors.
2) Restart metrics-forwarder if stuck: kubectl rollout restart deployment/metrics-forwarder --namespace=observability
3) If anomaly persists, escalate to Observability on-call.

Runbook hygiene: runbooks must include quick verification commands, rollback commands, owner, last_tested date, and link to a corresponding playbook in the team wiki.

---

5) Retrospective — Q2 2026 (summary & learnings)

Incidents tracked this quarter (high-level):
- I-2026-04-12: Hosted API p95 latency regression (root cause: kernel selection fallback on attention kernel after a Canaries rollout) — mitigation: rollback, hotfix to kernel selector. Time to mitigate (TTM): 42 minutes.
- I-2026-05-21: GPU pool partial outage in us-central1 due to host-level driver upgrade causing 4 nodes NotReady — mitigation: node replacement + autoscaler overlay. TTM: 1h 20m.
- I-2026-06-03: Metrics pipeline ingestion backlog after retention job misconfiguration — mitigation: increased retention window, backfill. TTM: 2h 5m.

Quantitative metrics (Q2 vs Q1):
- Mean monthly error rate: 0.08% (improved from 0.12%).
- p95 latency (hosted small models): 160ms (target 180ms).
- Number of P0 pages: 3 (Q1 had 5).
- Mean time to mitigate (P0): 54 minutes.

Key learnings and action items:
1) Kernel selection fallback must be exercised in canary tests. Action: add synthetic canary traffic that hits long-sequence paths. Owner: Runtime team (Sofia) — due 2026-08-01.
2) GPU node driver upgrades need staged rollout windows and canary nodes. Action: infra to run driver upgrades through a dedicated canary pool and automated rollback. Owner: GPU-fleet (Marcus) — due 2026-07-31.
3) Metrics pipeline alerting thresholds were too permissive. Action: tighten ingestion lag thresholds and add end-to-end synthetic metric assertions. Owner: Observability (Ravi) — due 2026-07-20.

Each action above must be tracked in the team backlog and included on the next on-call rotation review.

---

6) Roadmap & action items (next 2 quarters)

Major initiatives (owner — ETA):
- Observability hardening: tagging, retention, and cardinality control (Ravi Shah — Q3 2026 start, Q4 delivery).
- Automated canary bench for runtime kernels (Sofia Martinez — prototype by 2026-08-01).
- GPU fleet autoscaler enhancements (preemptible-aware scaling, better bin-packing) (Marcus Lee — rollout Q3 2026).
- Runbook automation: embed runbook steps as Prometheus alert runbook links with one-click remediation actions in Console (Aisha Patel — design by 2026-07-30).
- Platform cost telemetry: per-route cost breakdown and dynamic routing policy interface (Product + Platform — roadmap Q3–Q4 2026).

Backlog (short):
- Add cache hit ratio synthetic test to CI — owner: Platform-runtime — due 2026-07-10.
- Audit all dashboards for owner and runbook link — owner: Platform ops — due 2026-07-22.

7) Team wiki links and how-tos

Canonical how-tos (links):
- Runbooks index: /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks-index (maintain new runbooks here).
- How-to: add a new Grafana dashboard (documentation + checklist).
- How-to: create/modify Prometheus alert rules (includes test checklist and runbook annotation template).

How-to highlights:
- When adding an alert, always include: summary, impact, runbook_url, severity, and test plan.
- Tests: every new runbook must be validated in the next game day and have a last_tested tag in the runbook header.

---

Appendix: quick commands and useful queries

- Check API error rate (PromQL): sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="api",status!~"2.."}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="api"}[5m]))
- p95 latency (PromQL): histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="api"}[5m])) by (le))
- List recent deployments: kubectl get deploy -n redwood --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp | tail -n 20

Document maintenance:
- Owner (Aisha Patel) will review dashboards, alerts, and runbooks quarterly.
- All runbook changes must be peer-reviewed (at least one reviewer) and tested in the next scheduled game day.

If you have corrections or additions, open a PR in the docs repo and ping the reviewers list.
